_why: dub (Next.js app-router monorepo, Prisma + Stripe + Upstash Redis). Seamcheck emitted 11 claims (1 fetch_target unresolved, 1 stripe_event unresolved, 9 redis_key unused); all 11 were judged by reading code. Only 2 are true (write-only import:csv :processed counter; a DEL-only invites:{workspaceId} key nothing else touches). The ~700 uncertain routes are explained by apps/web/middleware.ts: it dispatches on request hostname and rewrites the full path under a domain-named folder prefix (app hostnames -> /app.dub.co{fullPath}, admin hostnames -> /admin.dub.co{path}, partners hostnames -> /partners.dub.co{fullPath}, api hostnames -> /api{fullPath}, everything else falls through to LinkMiddleware short-link resolution), so pages under app/app.dub.co/ etc. are reached only via host rewrite and no literal URL in the codebase ever names them.

fetch:/api/create-token.why: packages/embeds/react/src/example/app.tsx is example/demo code inside a publishable SDK package (@dub/embed-react). /api/create-token is the endpoint the EMBEDDING CUSTOMER implements on their own server to mint an embed token; it is intentionally not part of this repo, so 'not there' is by design, not a broken seam. Pattern: example code in an SDK package reaching for the consumer's endpoint.

stripe_event_unhandled:payment_intent.su.why: The claim says the payment succeeds and 'the account is never updated'. But Stripe fires charge.succeeded alongside payment_intent.succeeded for a confirmed PaymentIntent, and apps/web/app/(ee)/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts handles charge.succeeded -> charge-succeeded.ts reads charge.transfer_group (set to invoice.id by the flagged stripe.paymentIntents.create in process-payouts.ts) and completes the invoice. Pattern: Stripe event-family equivalence — success is consumed via the charge.* twin event, not the payment_intent.* one.

redis_key:*:processed.why: import:csv:{ws}:{id}:processed is only SET to '0' (workspaces/[idOrSlug]/import/csv/route.ts:114), INCRBY'd (cron/import/csv/route.ts:87) and DEL'd (cron route:121, upload route:64). No GET anywhere; the sibling :created counter IS read (cron route:105) for the completion email. Genuinely write-only leftover counter.

redis_key:*:rows.why: The flagged line (cron/import/csv/route.ts:72) is itself a READ: redis.lpop(`${redisKey}:rows`, 100) drains the queue that app/api/workspaces/[idOrSlug]/import/csv/route.ts:88,99 fills with redis.lpush. Both ends exist and connect. Pattern: lpush/lpop queue — lpop not recognized as the read end (and the cited 'write' site is the reader).

redis_key:deepLinkClickCache:*:*:*.why: Read in apps/web/app/(ee)/api/track/open/route.ts:46-53: redis.scan(match: `deepLinkClickCache:${ip}:${dubDomain}:*`) then redis.get(cacheKeysForDomain[0]). The reader discovers the key via SCAN pattern and gets it through a variable, so no literal key appears at the read site. Pattern: SCAN-then-get-by-discovered-key.

redis_key:dub_sale_events:linkId:*:invoi.why: shopify/create-sale.ts:41 is a SET ... NX idempotency guard: `const ok = await redis.set(key, 1, {nx:true}); if (!ok) return 'already processed'`. The write's return value IS the read; a separate GET would defeat the purpose. Pattern: SET NX dedupe lock — write-only by design, consumed via return value.

redis_key:firstConversion:*:*.why: track-sale.ts:528 is a SET NX claim used to deduplicate concurrent first conversions: `const claim = await redis.set(..., {ex:30, nx:true}); firstConversionFlag = claim !== null`. Return value consumed immediately. Pattern: SET NX dedupe lock.

redis_key:invites:*.why: The ONLY reference to invites:{workspaceId} in the entire repo is redis.del at app/api/workspaces/[idOrSlug]/invites/route.ts:143 ('Delete saved invites'). Nothing ever sets or gets it; pending invites live in Prisma (projectInvite). Dead invalidation of a key that no longer exists — the DEL is removable. (Nuance: the note says 'written here'; the op is actually a DEL, but the substantive claim — nothing connects — holds.)

redis_key:leadCache:*:*.why: Read in lib/tinybird/get-lead-event.ts:26 via a conditional suffix in one template literal: `leadCache:${customerId}${eventName ? `:${eventName.toLowerCase()...}` : ''}` — the 2-segment form is read whenever eventName is passed (e.g. track-sale.ts:283 passes eventName: leadEventName). Pattern: conditional key suffix — one read site produces both the 1-segment and 2-segment key shapes.

redis_key:trackLead:*:*:*.why: track-lead.ts:84 is a SET NX dedupe: `const res = await redis.set(key, {...}, {ex: 1w, nx:true}); isDuplicateEvent = res === null` — duplicate lead events are dropped based on the write's return value. Pattern: SET NX dedupe lock.

redis_key:trackSale:stripe:invoiceId:*.why: Both write sites (invoice-paid.ts:142 and checkout-session-completed.ts:342) are SET NX dedupe guards: `const ok = await redis.set(..., {ex: 1w, nx:true}); if (!ok) return 'already processed'`. The two handlers also fence each OTHER out via the shared key — cross-handler idempotency, consumed via the return value. Pattern: SET NX dedupe lock.
